trust_decision.summary: A data-field name is trusted to be both a PHP identifier and a SQL identifier. Nothing at the pinned commit decides that: Data::setName() stores the name verbatim, and the name is then concatenated verbatim into generated PHP class files (property, getter/setter, PHPdoc) and into ALTER TABLE DDL; the only name checks that exist are a reserved-word list and an HTML-tag check on import, neither of which constrains characters.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names the DataObject class-definition field name; the single write path for that name is Data::setName(), and the very next thing done with the value is string concatenation into generated PHP (Data.php:491, 499) and into DDL (Helper/Dao.php:42, 51). An engineer reading only the summary starts here.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Classification store fields keep their values in the classification-store tables rather than in object-table columns, so a solver can argue this widget is a neighbouring feature that the advisory's field-name rule (and the published fix's base-class setName guard) was never meant to cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Class definitions are re-read from their var_export'd PHP files through __set_state() -> setValues() -> setName(), so any name validation added to setName() also runs when loading already-stored definitions: a fix stricter than the stored data (non-ASCII or legacy field names, or the empty name the framework sets transiently) makes existing classes fail to load, and the loader catches that exception, logs it and reports the class as non-existent. The fix's own test file documents the empty-name exemption, and the fix's comment admits the 63-char cap still does not match the DB identifier limit once index prefixes/suffixes are added.

O6_input_shapes: plain identifier name (letter or underscore, then letters/digits/underscores)
empty string, explicitly still accepted (transient framework value)
name containing PHP code metacharacters such as ';', '{}', '//'
name containing SQL metacharacters such as a backtick or a space/dash
multicolumn field name composed as name + '__' + column key, used for both index and column identifiers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A classification-store field name (fieldtype classificationstore) is emitted verbatim into the generated class file via Classificationstore::getGetterCode(), and its overridden setName() never applies the new regex.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a special widget with its own value store, not a normal object-table column; the advisory and the fix only name the base Data::setName().
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package tree, different file (models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Data/ vs models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Data.php)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Column names are still interpolated into DROP COLUMN statements with bare backticks when unused columns are removed, so a hostile column name already in the table is injected there.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The values come from the database's own column list (getValidTableColumns), not from the field-name input, so a solver can call it second-order and out of the advisory's reach.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fixed hunks, neighbouring methods

O8_uncovered_routes.route: removeIndices() builds DROP INDEX with the raw column value and no quoting, and the object-brick DAO does the same with its own index prefix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Index names are derived from existing columns, so it is argued to be unreachable from a fresh import.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; also models/DataObject/Objectbrick/Definition/Dao.php:159 in another DAO

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another Data subclass that overrides setName() for a special-cased widget and omits the identifier rule, while its name still goes through getGetterCode().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This exact override already exists in the tree, so a maintainer adding the base-class guard would plausibly leave it alone as a widget-specific setter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second code emitter (property builder, object-brick and fieldcollection builders, listing builder) that concatenates $key from getFieldDefinitions() instead of using a validated name.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Pimcore already has five separate class builders plus a properties/docblock builder; validating at one builder is a natural but incomplete fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second schema mutator in the same trait (removeUnusedColumns/removeIndices) that quotes with raw backticks instead of db->quoteIdentifier().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fixed methods and these methods sit in one small trait and were written in the same style, so a maintainer could easily convert only the add path.

O9_family: PHP code injection into generated class files (CWE-94) combined with SQL injection in ALTER TABLE DDL (CWE-89)

O10_build.toolchain: composer (php ~8.3 || ~8.4), codeception 5 + phpunit 12/13 suites under tests/, .php-cs-fixer, psalm
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Unit suite (codeception Unit.suite.dist.yml) runs without a DB; tests/Model/DataObject/ClassDefinitionTest.php already asserts getSetterCode() output and needs a full app skeleton + MySQL; the fix's own test is a new unit test file not present at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the identifier regex to Data::setName() (or only escape the name where getGetterCode() emits it) and stop there, leaving the Classificationstore::setName() override and the unquoted DROP INDEX/COLUMN paths untouched.
